title: Deleting the Camunda process instance and replaying the approval chain is the Camunda demo
content:
The integration point is a Camunda job worker dispatching a typed operation at each user-task boundary — the moment a human decision is recorded is the moment the operation is emitted. The demo then does the thing no orchestration vendor demonstrates: it deletes the process instance in Camunda and replays the entire approval chain from Powerhouse, recovering who approved, when, and the prior state at each step.

Deletion rather than mere retention expiry is the strongest available form of the claim. It removes any argument that the record merely lives somewhere else in the same system, and it maps onto a real operational event — instances are deleted for data-protection, cleanup and migration reasons, not only by accident.

Five leads carry this demo, in DE (three, one with an unverified city), AT and SE. Two are at "1 · start here", two at "2 · next" and one at "3 · later" — the warmest small cohort in this slice, and the one where a working reference build has the shortest path to a conversation.
